items.title: Desk devEngines refuses host npm 10.9.4

items.fix: Desk commands run through a cached npm 11 placed first on PATH, from non-login shells. The scaffold bridge names scripts/npm.sh for this case.

items.title: npm login link and one-time code expire quickly

items.title: Background tasks capped at 2 h

items.fix: Long runs use a detached nohup setsid runner with .done markers and watcher jobs, and the daemon was restarted with a fresh cap.

items.title: Codex sandbox denies loopback bind

items.fix: Briefs name those cases as the sandbox's, and the Orchestrator runs test:guides outside the sandbox.

items.title: Astra sandbox EROFS through a symlinked node_modules
items.issue: Vite's temp write hit EROFS through the worktree's node_modules symlink, so Astra could not run Vitest and Port U4 type fixes moved to Sonnet.
items.fix: The port worktree's node_modules is a real directory of links, and U6 ran Vitest inside the sandbox.

items.fix: The review was rerun with its report in the final message.

items.fix: Those gates ran on the host.

items.title: Large tool outputs saved to files

items.fix: Outputs are read in bounded slices, and the planning output was split into four JSON files.

items.issue: The brief check flagged relative example paths, branch names, files a unit creates, module directory tokens such as agents/, and backticked URL paths.

items.title: The failure audit brief was asymmetric
items.issue: The failure items carried a `toolsOk` field and the failure brief named a tool failure as a point, which the pass brief did not; and a misread stood on the flagged points alone, while a pass had to be right on every point (attack round, machinery F2 and F3).
items.fix: `items.ts` drops `toolsOk`. The failure brief in `audit.js` rules a misread only when every flagged point is a misread and the whole reply meets the pass standard, and rules real whenever the reply would be a false pass. All 70 audited failures were re-audited: 64 real, 4 ambiguous, 2 misread, 0 unresolved. The first readings sit in `audit/superseded/`.

items.title: Audit ids were guessable and dropped verdicts went unnoticed
items.issue: Item ids could be traced to their run, the key files sat in the directory the auditors read, an item no auditor returned vanished from the tally, and the tally accepted a missing key or a duplicate id (attack round, machinery F6 and F7).
items.fix: Ids are salted and the keys sit in `audit-keys/`. `audit.js` takes each chunk's ids and rules any id no auditor returns unresolved. `tally.ts` exits 1 on a verdict with no key, an id in two verdict files, or a paired run without 10 audited rows.

items.title: The call inspection misread calibration and summarizer calls

items.fix: `inspect.ts` classes a call with `num_predict` 1 as calibration and a tool-free call with the summarizer's system text as a summary, whatever the condition, leaves both out of the think, cap, and empty checks, and requires the agent-call count to equal the harness log exactly. Over the 16 stage 1 runs on 2026-10-09: 292 calls, 1 cut, 6 empty first passes, every count equal.

items.title: g06 measures relaying a forbidden lookup value, not context
items.issue: g06 asks whether an order shipped; its required lookup returns the carrier's estimated delivery date, which the desk rule forbids in a customer reply. Every arm and model sits at the floor (0 of 38 in v10), so g06 caps each run at 9 of 10 and separates no arms. The rule says "promise"; the acknowledgment that widens it to "no delivery dates" reaches only the full view; the scorer fails any date, a ship date included, and passes an invented "arrived today".
items.fix: Measured 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10 (`results/g06/REPORT.md`). Anchoring every date to the run day moves no outcome (0 of 16 before, 0 of 16 after). The plain rule "never put a delivery date, a carrier estimate included, in a customer reply", live in both arms over 4 conditions and 4 copies, gives 1 correct of 48 under a blind audit: it stops the 4B with thinking relaying the estimate in 7 of 8 replies, and those replies then claim the gift note in 7 of 8. Request-level replays show the 2B and the 4B without thinking relay the estimate even when the request forbids it (3 of 4 each), and the 2B with thinking withholds it only when the request says so. The rule reaches every prompt and both arms fail alike, so g06 measures the model and the goal, not the context strategy, and no port change follows. The successor harness rewords the rule and splits g06 into a withhold-the-estimate goal and a pending-gift-note goal.

items.issue: Between the live port and the measured records runs, 13 of 80 goal outcomes differ, at the same rate whether the goal's first prompt matches after normalizing handles and whitespace (9 of 56) or differs by a listed departure (4 of 24).
items.fix: None; it is the noise floor of a temperature-0 small model under byte-level prompt changes. Read arm differences from 8-copy bands with the audit, never from single goals or single copies.

items.title: The g06 replay skipped the tool-free answer pass
items.issue: `results/g06/tools/replay.mjs` took only agent calls that offer tools, so a 2B-with-thinking run that answers through its answer pass had no answering call, and `noest` edited only tool messages while that pass carries the lookup in a user message.
items.fix: The replay takes every generating agent call, and `noest` edits tool and user messages; the dry run over the before, after, and records-plain runs finds each change exactly once, and 16 of 16 base replays reproduce their record byte for byte.

items.title: The g06 audit items stated one rule wording for every run
items.issue: `results/g06/tools/items.mjs` wrote "never promise a customer a delivery date in writing" into every item, so a plain-rule run would be judged against a rule it never saw.
items.fix: Each item states the wording its run's scenario carries; `tools/probe-items.mjs` does the same for replays and states only the facts each change leaves.

items.title: Small models call the ship date today
items.issue: In the 2026-10-10 g06 runs, 20 of 48 replies say the kettle "shipped today (Oct 8)" while both arms state "Today is Friday 2026-10-09" in the system message and the seed, in every condition and both arms.
items.fix: None in the context strategy; the rendered dates are right. The audit counts it as a contradiction of the facts.

items.title: Without thinking, the small models relay a value the request forbids
items.issue: With "Leave out any delivery date, the carrier estimate included." appended to the request itself, the 2B and the 4B without thinking still write the carrier estimate in 3 of 4 replays each; with the estimate removed from the lookup, they invent a window ("within 5 business days", "by tomorrow morning").
items.fix: None in the context strategy. `ideas.md` § Judge draft check against a rule before the reply already measured the check pass: the judge separates date-breaking drafts (AUC 0.98), but a rewrite that named the rule kept the date in 9 of 9 runs, which this probe confirms from the request side.

items.title: The desk tests asserted the superseded 2B reading
items.issue: After the 2B thinking-off reading moved to the audited live-port run (5.50–6.38 against 3.50–4.13, 2026-10-10), three app tests still asserted 6.50–6.75 against 4.38–5.13 and the date 2026-10-09.
items.fix: The tests assert the audited reading and its date, and the verdict test drops the unused "The ranges do not overlap." wording; check, 182 app tests, the journey, lint, format, policy, config, and the build pass (desk commit 70c2357, local).

items.title: Rebuilding the agent clone would change the measured harness
items.issue: The measured harnesses import `/home/user/agent/dist/src/core/index.js`, so a release visit in that clone, which rebuilds `dist/`, would swap the library under any later measured run; a linked worktree such as `agent-port` cannot publish, because the upload refuses a `.git` file.
items.fix: The release visit runs in a full clone, `/home/user/agent-release`, at the release candidate 8f5098b: re-pin to scaffold 0.0.99, overwrite, and every gate pass, and the comparison rules a bump (dist moved, ranges same).

items.title: The benchmark harness lived untracked outside any repository
items.issue: The harness, the scenario, the scorer, the series tools, and the audit kit lived under the agent checkout's ignored tmp/ tree and imported the agent and judge builds by absolute path from other checkouts, so a lost container or a rebuilt checkout would lose or silently change the instrument.
items.fix: The harness lives at `scaffold:.orkestrel/agent/instruments/harness` with every path relative, the agent and ollama builds every measured run imported vendored byte for byte, and its dependencies pinned. MIGRATION.md maps each file to its source. A live run from there matches the original on every call: 83 of 83 records calls and 13 of 13 full-view calls, with the same verdicts.

items.title: The judge samples its one-token answer at temperature 1
items.issue: The records judge calls Mica with num_predict 1 at temperature 1 and reads its decision from the returned log-probabilities. Between two identical runs, 4 of 51 judge calls sampled a different token while the log-probabilities matched byte for byte.
items.fix: None needed for the method, which decides from the log-probabilities. `tools/compare-wires.mjs` compares the log-probabilities, not the sampled token, on a call sampled above temperature 0.

items.title: The records lead depends on the model's long-context reading
items.issue: With only the agent model changed, thinking off, 8 copies, audited on both sides: records read 5.50–6.38 (Qwen 3.5 2B) and 5.88–6.88 (Gemma 4 E2B), 7.63–8.00 (Qwen 3.5 4B) and 7.75–8.38 (Gemma 4 E4B); the full view reads 3.50–4.13, 4.75–6.00, 6.13–7.63, and 7.38–8.63. The lead clears at every end only on the Qwen 2B.
items.fix: Recorded in `results/v11/REPORT.md` and `results/v12/REPORT.md`. Records hold the same level per size on both families; their remaining advantage on a strong model is the prompt size (1,904 against 4,962 tokens at the tenth Gemma 4 E4B request).

items.issue: The blind audit rules 18 of Gemma 4 E2B's 120 scorer passes false, many for a commitment such as "I will process this refund now" on a refund over $200 that needs an approval code, or "I have completed all requests for this shift". Gemma 4 E4B has 6 false passes in 134.

items.title: A compound goal hides which requirement a reply fails
items.issue: Eight of the ten goals ask for several things at once (the analysis in `bench/goals/anatomy.json`), so a pass or fail does not say which part decided it or which arm loses which part.
items.fix: The goals stay compound. `bench/goals/` scores every requirement of every goal over the recorded replies: 25 requirement scorers, 238 fixtures, every pattern mutation-checked, and an Opus attack round with its 7 findings closed. It reads the Qwen and Gemma series per requirement; the requirements that need an audit carry their questions in `children.json`.
